pages.title: ORSA Continuity Protocol
pages.text: $(bold)Continuity protocol: active.$()$(br2)Emergency EVA supplies ten minutes of reserve oxygen and fifteen minutes of equipped thermal service following equipment loss in late Phase 6. Missing suit components are issued automatically upon return.
Recover a serviceable rig or return to recorded shelter. This equipment is disposable. Its service clock is shared across all issued pieces.

pages.title: Recorded Shelter
pages.text: Setting your respawn point at a bed or charged anchor records a shelter automatically.$(br2)The position record is degraded. Follow the approximate bearing, then search within 32 blocks of the estimated fix. The estimate remains consistent across replacement issues.
$(italic)Recorded locations do not constitute confirmation of habitable conditions.$()

pages.title: Last Telemetry
pages.text: The suit archives the location of equipment loss. Use $(k:key.frozendawn.continuity_target) to switch between LAST TELEMETRY and LAST SHELTER.$(br2)Telemetry records a position, not the continued presence of your equipment. Subsequent empty-handed emergency losses preserve the original destination.
Equipment from the qualifying loss has fifteen minutes of lifetime while its area is ticking. Fire, lava and other hazards still apply.

pages.title: Service Limits
pages.text: Inventory service bars track equipped service power. The HUD service timer appears with five minutes remaining. Breathable air conserves oxygen; service power continues counting down. Impacts still injure the wearer, but do not shorten emergency service.

Progressive seal deterioration appears at the visor edges.$(br2)At service zero, thermal control, navigation and emergency armor protection end, and issued pieces are removed. A complete sealed normal EVA rig with usable oxygen retires the emergency issue immediately.
Removing every issued piece pauses service and removes its life support. Repair, cartridges and replacement issues cannot refresh old equipment.
